title: Merchant of Record Alternatives for Indian SaaS Businesses
summary: A SaaS founder in Bengaluru wants an alternative to their current Merchant of Record. The question sounds like a vendor swap. It is not. A cheaper checkout
body_markdown:
A SaaS founder in Bengaluru wants an alternative to their current Merchant of Record. The question sounds like a vendor swap. It is not. A cheaper checkout and an outsourced legal seller solve two different problems, and picking the wrong one creates work nobody budgeted for.


Merchant of Record alternatives for Indian SaaS businesses fall into three practical routes: another MoR service, direct card checkout, and invoice-led international bank collections. The first retains a third-party seller; the other two keep your Indian business as seller.


For eligible Indian SaaS businesses that want to sell directly,[Razorpay provides international payment collection](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/) through cards and bank transfers, with supported card subscriptions for recurring billing. Your customer mix and tax operating model determine which route belongs on your shortlist.


This guide explains seller identity, buyer experience, recurring billing, charges, settlement and export records, so you can choose an operating model before comparing offers.


### Key Takeaways


- Another MoR changes the service provider; it generally retains the external seller-of-record arrangement.
- Direct card checkout suits SaaS businesses that want to remain the seller and can manage their applicable tax obligations.
- Razorpay is a relevant direct-collection shortlist option for eligible Indian SaaS businesses selling overseas, including supported international-currency card subscriptions.
- Invoice-led bank collection addresses buyers who pay against contracts and invoices. It is a different workflow from self-serve card renewal.
- Assess processing, currency conversion, billing and tax tools, refunds and operational effort together. A gateway fee and a bundled MoR service are different scopes.
- Confirm approval, supported currencies, settlement terms, and the exact remittance documents for your selected flow.


## What Are the Merchant of Record Alternatives for Indian SaaS?


An Indian SaaS business can retain a third-party seller through another MoR, become the direct seller using card checkout, or collect invoice payments through international bank transfers. Shortlist the model by tax ownership and buyer workflow. For the direct-selling routes, evaluate Razorpay’s international collection products against your account eligibility and billing requirements.


The common mistake is treating these as three interchangeable payment processors. They are three purchasing routes with different legal consequences. Tax automation software can sit on top of direct collection to help with calculation and reporting, but it is a supporting layer, not a fourth seller model. A tax engine does not register on your behalf, does not remit in most setups, and does not absorb your liability.


### Compare Seller Identity Before Comparing Providers


Route Who sells to the end buyer? Suitable starting situation What you still need to verify Razorpay relevance


Another MoR service External MoR under its contract You want covered buyer-tax and billing administration handled by a seller-of-record service Product and country eligibility, covered taxes, fees, reserves and migration rights Separate category; this guide does not establish availability of Razorpay’s waitlisted MoR service


Direct international card checkout Your Indian SaaS business Self-serve purchases or supported recurring card subscriptions, with tax operations arranged International activation, currencies, subscription capabilities, fees and retained tax duties Razorpay International Payments and supported Subscriptions


Invoice-led international bank collection Your Indian SaaS business Annual contracts, enterprise procurement or buyers who prefer bank transfers Supported transfer rail, buyer details, invoice matching, fees and documentation Razorpay International Bank Transfer / MoneySaver Export Account


### Shortlist by Buyer Workflow


Seller identity is the first filter. Buyer workflow is the second.


- **Monthly self-serve buyer paying by card:** compare direct checkout with an MoR based on who will administer covered transaction taxes.
- **Annual B2B buyer paying an invoice:** evaluate bank collections before assuming card checkout is the only alternative to an MoR.
- **Mixed Indian and overseas audience:** evaluate each buyer flow separately. Overseas customers do not automatically require an MoR, and domestic UPI availability does not establish foreign-currency UPI support.


One more filter belongs before pricing: seller-country eligibility. Some MoR products restrict which countries a seller can be incorporated in. Confirm that an India-incorporated entity can onboard before you compare rate cards.


### Did You Know?


Changing the collection rail does not, by itself, change who the legal seller is.


## When Should an Indian SaaS Business Shortlist Razorpay?


Shortlist Razorpay when your Indian SaaS business wants direct international collection and has a plan for its applicable tax obligations. Its documented options include international cards, supported card subscriptions and invoice-led bank transfers. The benefit is a collection choice matched to how your buyers pay, while your business retains the seller relationship. Activation and product eligibility apply.


### International Card Checkout for Self-Serve SaaS


The underlying task is simple to describe. An overseas customer pays for access to your software. Your Indian business contracts with the buyer, invoices the buyer and receives the money.


Razorpay documents[international payment options](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/) for this flow. The documentation states that an eligible, registered business with a valid website can accept international payments via cards issued by domestic or foreign banks, and PayPal, subject to an active account with KYC verification completed and published terms, privacy, refund and cancellation policies.


Take a hypothetical $49 monthly plan as an illustration only. A customer in Berlin reaches your pricing page, selects the plan, pays by card in a supported currency, and gains access. No approval rate or net settlement amount is promised by that example. Activation is a real step: Razorpay’s guidance explains that full domestic activation comes first, and that invoices, bank statements, FIRS/FIRA records and prior settlement reports help secure banking-partner approval.


Where you need a hosted payment request rather than a full checkout build,[Payment Links](https://razorpay.com/payment-links/) can serve that purpose. A one-time payment link does not automatically create a recurring subscription.


### Supported International Card Subscriptions


Razorpay’s Subscriptions documentation supports subscription payments in supported international currencies through cards. This gives an eligible SaaS business a direct recurring-collection option for overseas customers. The[Subscriptions FAQ](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs/) states that you can accept subscription payments in supported currencies, that only card payments support international currencies, and that[UPI payments do not](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs/?preferred-country=IN) .


Confirm international activation, the customer’s payment method and your required billing features before selecting the setup. The same documentation notes that UPI supports only INR, with recurring UPI AutoPay transactions capped at Rs 15,000 for standard categories (and Rs 1,00,000 for select categories such as mutual funds, insurance premiums, and credit card repayments, effective 1 January 2024), and[eMandate via NetBanking supports only INR](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs) . Domestic mandate availability does not establish foreign-currency recurring support.


### INR Settlement and Invoice-Led Collection


For the documented card-subscription flow, foreign-currency payments settle in INR. The Subscriptions FAQ states that[settlements are always made in INR, with the payment converted using the exchange rate at the time of payment creation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs/?preferred-country=IN) . The customer-facing currency and the currency received in your Indian bank account are separate choices.


If an enterprise buyer prefers to pay an invoice by bank transfer, evaluate Razorpay International Bank Transfer as a separate collection route, rather than treating every SaaS payment as a card checkout.


> **Pro Tip:** Ask Product or Sales to validate one representative buyer journey end to end, along with your needed billing features. An account approval is not proof that every currency or payment method is enabled.


## Who Handles Tax and Export Records When You Use Razorpay?


With Razorpay’s direct collection products, your SaaS business remains the seller and must arrange its applicable tax compliance. Razorpay supplies payment collection and documented remittance-record workflows; those do not make the gateway your global tax seller. Direct collection is a practical choice when your finance team, advisers and supporting tools can manage the responsibilities that stay with you.


That responsibility is not theoretical. In *Consumption Tax Trends 2024* , the OECD reports that over 100 jurisdictions globally have already enacted reforms based on its VAT/GST guidelines, with roughly 30 more in the process of doing so or considering reform. That structural shift is why the MoR category exists at all.


### Make the Responsibility Split Specific


Task Direct collection with Razorpay An MoR arrangement


Contract and invoice to the end buyer Your SaaS business, according to the sales arrangement Check the MoR’s reseller contract and invoice issuer


Applicable buyer-country indirect taxes Your business arranges assessment, registration, collection and filing where required Provider handles the taxes and transactions covered by its contract


Indian business tax and export analysis Remains a merchant responsibility, with professional advice as needed Indian supplier obligations still need assessment


Payment and remittance records Use the documents available for the selected Razorpay flow and reconcile them to invoices Confirm the payout records and supplier-to-MoR relationship


### Use the Correct Remittance Document


Razorpay’s[FIRS documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/account-settings/firs/) distinguishes bank-provided certificates from Razorpay-generated statements and describes downloadable records[based on your monthly transactions](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/account-settings/firs/?preferred-country=IN) . Keep those records with invoices and settlement references, and confirm which document your accountant or Authorised Dealer bank needs. Do not assume every card payment produces a separate bank-issued eFIRC.


Export treatment is a facts-and-documents question. IGST Act section 2(6) sets multiple conditions that must be satisfied together, including the prescribed manner of payment receipt. A remittance statement alone does not establish tax treatment. Equally, an MoR arrangement does not automatically invalidate export treatment, and a gateway does not automatically guarantee GST or FEMA compliance.


## How Do You Compare MoR, Card Checkout and Bank Collection Costs?


Compare the amount your business retains after processing, currency conversion, billing and tax tools, refunds and operating effort. An MoR quote may bundle services that a gateway quote does not include. For Razorpay, request the applicable commercial terms for cards and bank transfers separately, then reconcile a sample payment from customer charge to bank receipt.


### Separate Processing Fees From Currency Conversion


Razorpay’s[currency conversion documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/currency-conversion/) states that settlements occur in INR based on the conversion rate at the time of payment, and that the exchange rate according to the processing bank on the date the payment was made is used to make the conversion, with the worked example settling the converted amount minus taxes and fees.


Review that rate alongside your agreed processing charges to understand the amount received. Confirm your applicable terms rather than treating an online estimate as a quote. Bank-transfer pricing is a separate offer and cannot be applied to cards.


Timing matters as much as rate. The settlements documentation notes that[the default settlement cycle for international payments is as per applicable laws and is visible on the Razorpay Dashboard](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/settlements/?preferred-country=IN) , so treat settlement timing as account-dependent.


On the MoR side, headline percentages rarely tell the whole story. As of late 2026, published base rates across major MoR providers typically range from 2.9% + $0.30 up to 5% + $0.50, with international card and subscription surcharges stacking on top depending on the provider.


### Compare Equivalent Service Scope


Cost or obligation What to record before choosing


Processing Percentage and fixed component; card or transfer rail; approved account terms


FX Conversion rate, timestamp, markup if applicable, and settlement currency


Additional tools Billing, tax assessment, calculation, filing and reconciliation costs outside the payment quote


Exceptions Refund and dispute terms, reserves, holds and any payout charges


Operating effort Finance and engineering work required to run this model month after month


> **Pro Tip:** Compare one monthly self-serve card payment and one annual invoice side by side. Different ticket sizes and buyer workflows can justify different collection routes within the same business.


## Can Direct Card Subscriptions Support Global SaaS Billing?


A direct card-subscription setup can support recurring international collection where the account, currency and card are supported. That capability is separate from pricing plans, usage metering, entitlements, tax invoicing and revenue recognition. Validate the features your SaaS actually needs before moving a live subscriber base.


### Validate the Subscription Lifecycle


Treat sign-up, first collection, renewal, failed payment, cancellation and entitlement update as distinct events, each with its own failure mode. A subscriber who renews successfully for eleven months and fails in month twelve is a dunning problem, not a checkout problem.


A documented card-subscription product does not guarantee that every overseas issuer will authorise every renewal. Issuer behaviour varies by country, card type and risk signals.


Confirm whether your commercial model is flat-rate, seat-based, usage-based or annual invoicing, then check each requirement against current documentation. Use[Razorpay Subscriptions](https://razorpay.com/subscriptions/) for product discovery and the[Subscriptions FAQ](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs/) for payment-method and currency scope.


### Keep Payment Collection and Product Entitlements in Sync


Billing and access drift apart quietly. A cancelled subscription that leaves a seat active, or a failed renewal that locks out a paying customer, both cost more than the transaction fee.


Ask the implementation team to validate billing notifications and cancellation behaviour against current documentation. Then specify a test matrix covering supported card and currency, renewal, failure, refund and access update. This is a validation recommendation, not a claim that integration tests have already passed.


Do not assume stored payment credentials transfer between providers. Mandate and credential portability require approval from both platforms and a verified migration plan.


### Did You Know?


A monthly subscription can be charged in a supported foreign currency while the documented settlement reaches the merchant in INR.


## When Are Invoice-Led International Bank Collections the Better Fit?


Invoice-led bank collection is worth evaluating when a SaaS buyer purchases through a contract, purchase order or annual invoice and prefers a bank transfer. The Indian SaaS business remains the seller. Razorpay[International Bank Transfer](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/international-bank-transfer/) documents local currency collection options, invoice management and settlement workflows for eligible exporters, including SaaS businesses.


### Match an Enterprise Payment to Its Invoice


Picture a hypothetical annual contract with a procurement-led buyer. Your team issues a commercial invoice with a unique reference. The buyer’s finance team pays into the supported local-currency collection account using a familiar domestic rail. The incoming payment carries the reference, which your finance team matches to the invoice, then to the settlement record in your Indian bank account.


Receipt into a virtual collection account and final availability in your merchant bank account are separate events. Reconcile both.


Deal size can also drive the rail choice. RBI’s Master Direction states that in respect of inward or outward transactions processed by a PA-CB, the maximum value per transaction shall be Rs 25 lakh. That is per transaction, not cumulative, and a large annual enterprise invoice can bump into it.


### Check the Rail, Activation and Documentation


- Current documentation describes collection through local currency accounts with virtual accounts in several markets,[receiving via ACH, FPS, SEPA, NPP, EFT and SWIFT](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/accept-international-payments-via-swift-transfer/?preferred-country=IN) . Availability depends on the collection setup and approved account.
- Prerequisites include an active Razorpay account with KYC verification completed, business PAN provided during onboarding, and membership of a listed export purpose code. Other activation requirements may apply.
- A bank-transfer instruction is not a recurring card mandate. Any debit collection feature requires its own eligibility and authorisation review.
- Ask for the applicable fee, conversion basis, settlement trigger, and remittance document. Do not apply a card fee or a domestic settlement claim to this flow.


> **Pro Tip:** Include the invoice identifier and buyer details required by the collection workflow from the beginning. Reconciliation works best when those fields are designed before the buyer sends funds.


## When Should You Retain a Merchant of Record?


Retain or replace an MoR when you want a third party to act as seller for covered transactions and administer the buyer-facing taxes and billing services in its contract. This can suit a SaaS team that values outsourced commerce administration more than direct seller control. Review the actual coverage, payout terms and migration constraints rather than assuming every responsibility transfers.


### Evaluate the Contracted Service


- Who appears as seller on the invoice and the customer’s card statement?
- Which product types, buyer locations and tax obligations are actually covered by the contract?
- Who bears refund and chargeback amounts, and when can balances be reserved or recovered?
- What data and subscription export rights are available at exit?
- Which records support the Indian supplier’s accounting and export analysis?


Provider continuity deserves a place on that list. The category has seen a documented wind-down: one widely used MoR platform has stated that sign-ups are closed and the platform will shut down on March 31, 2027. Ask what happens to active subscriptions, stored credentials and outstanding balances if a provider exits or pauses your account after a risk review.


### Use a Mixed Setup Only When It Solves a Defined Need


A conditional architecture can work. Run an MoR for a covered market where outsourced administration genuinely saves effort, and direct collection for a separate eligible segment whose tax operations you already manage.


If you do, define how the business reconciles two systems and how it identifies the seller for each sale. Revenue reporting, invoice numbering and customer support all need a single source of truth.


Do not make “MoR for all overseas customers, Razorpay only for India” the default recommendation. Equally, do not claim every SaaS team should replace its MoR with a gateway. Buyer requirements, tax capability and commercial terms determine the fit.


## How Do You Move From an MoR to Direct SaaS Collections?


Move to direct collections only after validating your tax operating model, payment activation, billing lifecycle and customer migration requirements. Start with a limited segment, reconcile invoices to receipts and keep a fallback. Do not assume existing mandates or stored payment credentials can transfer between providers.


1. **Map the present seller and contract.** Identify the MoR’s role, notice period, payout balance, refund obligations and data-export rights. Get the exit terms in writing first.
2. **Choose the direct-selling segment.** Specify B2B or B2C, buyer countries, contract sizes, billing frequency and card versus invoice preference. A narrow first segment is easier to reconcile.
3. **Arrange tax and export operations.** Have finance and advisers assess the relevant registrations, invoicing, filing and export records before you collect directly. This step gates the rest.
4. **Confirm Razorpay product eligibility.** Validate international activation, currencies, collection methods, approved commercials and required documentation for that segment. The[activation requirements guide](https://razorpay.com/learn/breaking-down-the-requirements-for-accepting-international-payments-through-razorpay/) sets out what supporting evidence helps.
5. **Validate billing and access behaviour.** Test sign-up, renewal or invoice payment, failure, refund, cancellation and product-entitlement updates against current documentation.
6. **Plan customer communication and consent.** Confirm whether re-authorisation is required, explain any seller or statement-descriptor change, and build safeguards against duplicate billing during the overlap window.
7. **Pilot and reconcile.** Match invoices, gross payments, conversion, fees, taxes, settlement references and remittance records on a controlled cohort. Set acceptance criteria with finance and engineering before the pilot starts.
8. **Expand after the pilot meets the criteria.** Retain rollback arrangements and any outstanding MoR obligations. Review payment failures, reconciliation effort and customer queries before broadening the migration.


Assign internal ownership explicitly: Product and Engineering for the lifecycle tests, Finance and Compliance for tax, records and acceptance criteria. For a deeper implementation view, see the[migration guide for international payment gateways](https://razorpay.com/blog/international-payment-gateway-migration/) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What Are the Main Merchant of Record Alternatives for Indian SaaS Businesses?


Another MoR service retains a third-party seller arrangement. Direct card checkout and invoice-led international bank collection keep your Indian business as seller. Choose by buyer workflow, tax operating capacity, billing needs, and total cost, then compare providers within the chosen category rather than across categories.


### Can I Use Razorpay for International SaaS Subscriptions?


Razorpay’s[Subscriptions FAQ](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs/) documents card payments in supported international currencies. Eligibility, international activation and payment-method support apply. Verify required billing features and the full lifecycle before migrating subscribers. Domestic UPI or eMandate availability should not be read as foreign-currency recurring support.


### Does Razorpay Handle My Overseas VAT and Sales Tax as Part of Direct Collection?


No. Direct collection does not transfer your seller tax obligations to the gateway. Arrange the assessment and administration of applicable taxes through your finance team, advisers and supporting tools. If you need an external legal seller for covered transactions, evaluate an MoR service and its contract separately.


### Should Annual SaaS Contracts Use Cards or International Bank Transfers?


Start with the buyer’s procurement and payment preference. Cards can suit self-serve collection; invoice-led bank transfers can suit negotiated annual contracts, particularly where ticket sizes are large. Compare the applicable rails, fees, conversion, invoice matching, timing and documents for your approved account.


### Is Direct Collection Always Cheaper Than an MoR?


No universal savings are established. Compare equivalent service scope, including processing, FX, billing, tax tools, exceptions and staff effort. A lower payment fee can still come with additional operating work. Obtain current terms and reconcile a representative payment before deciding.
